Class enumeration and comparison of mixture models

Source: R/enumeration.R
enumerate_classes.Rd

enumerate_classes() fits every candidate in a grid of class counts (and, for continuous indicators, covariance structures) and collects their information criteria, classification quality and estimation diagnostics in one object. It covers latent profile, latent class and latent transition models, single-level or two-level, and the additive, dispersion and additive-dispersion families of multilpa(). The fitted candidates stay in the result (see Value).

Information criteria summarise relative support; entropy and average posteriors describe classification certainty within each candidate. Neither picks a solution: also check that the best likelihood was replicated across starts, that no estimate sits at a bound, and that an added class brings interpretable differences in the response patterns. More profiles can stand in for covariances a diagonal structure cannot hold, so compare class counts alongside plausible structures. The grid is the analyst's: when every criterion is lowest at its edge, extend it.

Usage

enumerate_classes(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles = 1:4,
  n_group_classes = 1:3,
  model = "basic",
  seed = NULL,
  family = "profiles",
  between_variance = c("varying", "equal"),
  time = NULL,
  ...,
  cores = 1L,
  type = NULL,
  verbose = cores > 1L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per observation: the indicators, the group identifier and, when used, the occasion column and covariates. Use the same rows and scale for every candidate.

vars

Names of the indicator columns.

id

The column identifying the groups the rows are nested in. NULL enumerates single-level models, with a message; enumerate_lpa() and enumerate_lca() do that directly.

n_profiles

Profile (class) counts to try (default 1:4; 2:4 for transition models).

n_group_classes

Group-class counts to try (default 1:3; default 1 with time, and only 1 with id = NULL).

model

Covariance structures to cross with the class counts. "basic" (the default for profile grids) fits EEI (equal variances, no covariances), VVI (varying variances), EEE (one covariance matrix shared by all profiles) and VVV (a covariance matrix per profile). "all" fits all fourteen structures. Otherwise mclust's three-letter codes (volume, shape and orientation, each equal E or varying V, I for no covariances), or NULL for none, which is the default for a transition grid. With one continuous indicator, codes that coincide are fitted once; with only categorical indicators no structure is crossed. Giving variance_model, covariance_model, volume, shape or orientation in ... sets one structure instead.

seed

Optional integer seed, reproducing the starting values for the same data and controls.

family

"profiles" (default) enumerates the profile model over n_profiles, n_group_classes and model. One or more of "additive", "dispersion" and "additive_dispersion" enumerates those group-class families over family, n_group_classes and between_variance instead; they need id, refuse n_profiles and model, and return a latents_family_enumeration.

between_variance

For the group-class families, the restrictions to cross: "varying", "equal" or both (default). The dispersion family is fitted with "equal" only.

time

The occasion column. Enumerates latent transition models (lta()) over n_profiles and n_group_classes, every other lta() argument in ... held fixed; model, when given, crosses structures. Profile family only; returns a latents_transition_enumeration.

...

Further arguments of multilpa(), or of lta() with time, used for every candidate: typically n_starts, max_iter, missing, categorical, centering, scaling, drop_empty and boundary. The group-class families take only n_starts, max_iter, tol and min_variance.

cores

Maximum number of parallel workers (default 1, serial). With seed, parallel and serial runs give the same result. On Windows, and on macOS with Apple's Accelerate BLAS, each worker is a separate R process, so memory grows with cores.

type

"lca", "lpa" or "lta"; NULL (default) reads the type from the other arguments. "lca" treats every indicator as categorical, numeric codes included, as multilca() does (indicators in ordinal or count keep those distributions, and categorical adds to the set). "lpa" needs continuous indicators and no categorical, ordinal or count. Both need time = NULL. "lta" needs time and reads the measurement from categorical, as lta() does, without making numeric indicators categorical. An explicit type needs family = "profiles".

verbose

Whether to report progress: one message each when the candidates are prepared, when starts are screened, when they are fitted and when the grid is done. Default on when cores > 1. Not reported for the group-class families.

Value

A multilpa_enumeration object, or the transition or family enumeration named under time and family; the print header names the resolved type (LPA, LCA, LTA, mixed or family). On every grid: get_candidates() gives one row per candidate (named like "profiles3_groups2") with its class counts, log likelihood, criteria, entropy, convergence, boundary and replication, leaving out columns empty in every row; get_best() the best candidate per criterion; get_tree() and plot_tree() how classes split; get_entropy(), get_avepp() and get_classification() the classification tables of every candidate; plot_criteria() the criteria; get_candidate() one fitted candidate; compare_models() candidates by name (a family grid is compared in its own candidates table). A profile or class grid also has the AvePP summaries at each level in its candidates table, get_deltas() and get_knees(), and a summary() that prints one screen of the evidence; a transition or family grid's summary() is its candidates table. Invalid arguments are refused with the classed conditions listed on latents-conditions.

See also

get_candidate(), bootstrap_lrt() to test one class count against the next, enumerate_regressions() for mixture regressions.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:10, each = 10), y = rnorm(100))
candidates <- enumerate_classes(d, "y", "g", n_profiles = 1:2,
                              n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
as.data.frame(candidates)

# Numeric response codes, explicitly categorical:
codes <- data.frame(g = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10), item = rep(0:1, 50))
classes <- enumerate_classes(codes, "item", "g", type = "lca",
                             n_profiles = 1, n_group_classes = 1,
                             n_starts = 1, seed = 1)

# Single level, crossing class counts with two named structures:
single <- enumerate_lpa(iris, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width",
                                "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"),
                        n_profiles = 1:3, model = c("VVV", "EEE"),
                        n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
summary(single)
